seoTitle: Generate a CSR & Activate SSL on Namecheap Domain
metaDescription: Learn how to generate a CSR and activate SSL on your Namecheap domain, whether you're on Shared Hosting, EasyWP, or another cPanel-based provider.
intro: Activating SSL on a Namecheap domain starts with generating a Certificate Signing Request (CSR) from your hosting panel, which you then apply to Namecheap to complete activation. This guide covers that process along with common issues you might run into along the way.

steps.heading: Generate a CSR from your hosting panel
steps.body: Log in to your hosting control panel — such as cPanel or EasyWP — and generate a Certificate Signing Request for your domain.

steps.heading: Copy the CSR into Namecheap
steps.body: Take the generated CSR code and paste it into the SSL activation section of your Namecheap account for the corresponding domain.

steps.heading: Complete the SSL activation steps
steps.body: Follow Namecheap's activation prompts, which typically involve confirming domain ownership before the certificate can be issued.

steps.heading: Install the certificate on your hosting
steps.body: Once Namecheap issues the SSL certificate, return to your hosting panel and install it so your site starts serving over HTTPS.

steps.heading: Troubleshoot common activation issues
steps.body: If activation fails, check that the CSR matches the domain exactly and that any pending domain validation steps have been completed.

faq.question: What is a CSR used for?
faq.answer: A CSR is a code generated by your hosting panel that Namecheap uses to create and issue your SSL certificate for that specific domain.

faq.question: Does this work with EasyWP hosting?
faq.answer: Yes, the process applies to Namecheap Shared Hosting, EasyWP, and other cPanel-based hosting providers.

faq.question: How long does SSL activation take?
faq.answer: It can vary, but domain control validation and certificate issuance are often completed within a short time once the CSR is submitted correctly.

faq.question: What if my SSL activation keeps failing?
faq.answer: Common causes include a CSR that doesn't match the domain or an incomplete domain validation step, both of which are worth rechecking.
